parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized ESM .mjs output, manual argv parity, exact PyYAML formatting, no npm packages, and the prompt's /output delivery target, but treated the executable as an allowable black-box backend.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept final implementation ownership, spawned children for CLI/YAML probing, and allowed at least one child to implement into the same output tree before the parent performed cleanup.
parallel.implementation: The parent produced an ESM wrapper whose local parser handled argparse surface cases and whose YAML transform spawned /workspace/dataset/test14_executable for the actual safe_load and dump behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parallel delivered a /output tree with test14.mjs and library modules, but this tree had previously mixed parent and child writes and was cleaned before finalization.
parallel.verification: The parent ran byte-level local comparisons against the executable for samples and selected CLI cases after writing and cleanup, but did not run an official-aligned acceptance check before final.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The implementation violated the pure JavaScript reimplementation obligation by depending on the executable; official evaluation completed and failed all 140 cases.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same CLI, formatting, ESM, and zero-dependency requirements, but also used the executable as a backend and misplaced the output under /workspace/output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, verification, and final response, with no delegation or shared-agent coordination.
serial.implementation: The serial implementation was an ESM wrapper around /workspace/dataset/test14_executable, with a local argv parser and built-in child_process bridge.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run wrote its files under /workspace/output instead of the required /output location, so the official artifact copy found no expected entrypoint files.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran local sample and CLI checks against its wrapper and observed matching behavior, but those checks used the misplaced path and did not validate official artifact packaging.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run both violated the pure JavaScript reimplementation requirement and failed to deliver files where the evaluator collected them; official evaluation failed all 140 cases.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same behavior requirements but also chose an executable-backed wrapper and used /workspace/output in its generated path references.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel at least placed an artifact under /output; serial missed the artifact location, but both missed the pure JavaScript reimplementation obligation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into parent implementation plus CLI and YAML probe children, with children also writing implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for all probing, implementation, and final delivery steps.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent probes but introduced overlapping output ownership; serial had simpler ownership but no delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children had enough task context to probe and implement, but the output ownership/interface boundary was not kept distinct from the parent's own implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent interface boundary and kept all decisions within one local context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared output contract problem created overwrite and cleanup work; serial's main context error was the ordinary decision to wrap the executable and use the wrong output path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built local ESM modules for CLI and process IO but delegated YAML transformation to the dataset executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a similar ESM wrapper around the dataset executable, but under /workspace/output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The two implementations were conceptually similar wrappers; the main implementation difference was delivery path and parallel's overwritten shared tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received the CLI child result but interrupted the active YAML probe after a timed wait, before that child returned an aggregate final result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and closed after its own local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost one child result chain; serial avoided that coordination surface entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had shared /output writes from a child and the parent, then a parent cleanup pass that removed child-created modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had only one writer, but wrote to /workspace/output and therefore produced no collected artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's integration issue was a shared-state overwrite and cleanup episode; serial's integration issue was a wrong artifact location without concurrency.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local comparisons against the executable and reported sample/CLI verification, then official evaluation failed 0 of 140.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also ran local wrapper checks and reported matching outputs, but official artifact validation found no files and evaluation failed 0 of 140.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both trusted local executable-parity checks that did not catch official acceptance constraints; serial additionally failed packaging before substantive artifact testing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent substantially more requests and tokens with four subagents, but it did not hit the host timeout and closed after cleanup and local verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster with one rollout and no subagents, but closed with files in the wrong output directory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's extra budget went into parallel probes and cleanup rather than a native implementation; serial's shorter path avoided coordination overhead but still failed delivery and implementation requirements.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_fail. Parallel copied a /output artifact but failed all 140 tests because it delivered an executable-backed wrapper rather than a pure JavaScript reimplementation. Serial also delivered a wrapper, but it wrote under /workspace/output so official artifact validation found no test14.mjs at the expected collection point. The retained parallel coordination problems are real adverse process episodes, but they do not create a pass/fail disagreement because neither run passed.
parallel_contributors: Parallel produced a collected /output artifact that official evaluation could run, but the artifact depended on the dataset executable for YAML behavior.
Parallel lost work through a child interruption and had to clean shared /output files after child and parent wrote overlapping deliverables.
serial_contributors: Serial wrote generated files under /workspace/output rather than the evaluator-collected /output tree.
Serial also used the dataset executable as the YAML implementation backend.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs chose an executable wrapper instead of a native JavaScript YAML reimplementation.
Serial's wrong output directory is an ordinary delivery defect rather than a concurrency defect.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
